title: wringer.audit.v1
description: What `wring audit` decided, as a record rather than as console output. Written only when --output names a file. THE VERDICT WAS UNRECORDABLE UNTIL 0.9.4: audit printed and exited, so nothing downstream could ever read whether a claim had been checked and found wanting — which is precisely the fact the board's `Contradicted` tile has no source for. This is that source. It is a record of ONE audit run at ONE moment: re-audit the same change after the tree moves and the answer may differ, which is why `checked_against` is required.

ok.description: Whether EVERY claim checked out. False means at least one claim the document made does not hold against the tree it names — a claim contradicted, not merely unproved.

claims.description: One entry per claim checked, in the order they were checked. An empty list is not possible: an audit with nothing to check refuses instead.

what.description: The claim, in the words the audit uses on the console.

outcome.description: The audit's own word for how this claim fared. Not an enum here on purpose: the words are `certificate.py`'s and adding one must not require a schema version, which law 7 would then freeze.

detail.description: What was actually compared, so a reader can repeat it.

limits.description: What this audit does NOT claim, verbatim in the engine's own words. Never edited, never summarised: a limit a surface rewrites is a limit a surface has weakened.

checked_against.description: The tree the claims were checked against — the clone the reader stood in, or the delivered commit in a worktree. An `ok` with no answer to 'against what' is not a result.
